engine: QuickJS compiled to WASM (quickjs-wasi 3.6.3, embedded in the package), a fresh QuickJS context per run inside a pooled Node worker thread
how_run: run({ source, hostFunctions: { host: { lookup } } }) for the default configuration and createRunner({ limits }).run(...) for the hardened one, both from the package entry point; guest code calls host.lookup({id}).

P2.detail: The caller gets only the return value. A bare last expression returns undefined (the source is a function body), so P2 as written returns nothing; P2b with `return "RETURNED"` returns it. console.log never reaches the caller: it is written with writeSync to the host's fd 1. defaults.time: timeoutMs 30,000 wall for the whole invocation; cpuTimeoutMs 10,000 of guest execution, enforced by a QuickJS interrupt handler (packages/run/src/types.ts:64-88, runtime/worker.ts:207-235). The CPU limit fires first for a busy loop.
defaults.memory: memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB QuickJS heap, maxStackSizeBytes 2 MiB (types.ts:89-92, runtime/worker.ts:514-534)
defaults.output: maxResultBytes 1 MiB for the return value (fails, not truncates); maxConsoleOutputBytes 64 KiB, but console output goes to host stdout and never to the caller (types.ts:93-96, runtime/worker.ts:662-690)
defaults.tool_calls: maxBridgeRequests 256 total and maxInFlightBridgeRequests 32 concurrent; exceeding either fails the run with RUN_BRIDGE_LIMIT (types.ts:103-106, runtime/manager.ts:995-1003)

source_notes.finding: Host functions are passed as named groups; each group becomes a guest global object whose members are callable (`host.lookup(...)`). There are no top-level functions and no generated declarations: Run is an execution layer and leaves prompts and types to the caller.
None in Run itself. No type generation or search code exists in packages/run/src (grep for declaration or JSON Schema generation finds nothing). The AI SDK code mode layer adds it.

Each host call goes from the QuickJS context to __runInvokeHostFunction in the worker, which posts a request to the manager on the main thread and returns a guest promise; the manager runs the host function and posts the result back. Async calls overlap, which is why P9 is parallel. An optional synchronous bridge (syncHostFunctions) uses a separate shared-memory protocol.

QuickJS WASM in a Node worker thread, fresh context per run, worker reused. Guest hardening deletes Node-style globals and replaces Function and eval with throwing stubs. The docs say plainly that this is not a container, VM or separate OS process. The worker is created with a copy of process.env, but nothing in the guest can read it (P5).

Only the return value comes back (RunCompletedResult has status and value). console.* writes with writeSync to the host process's fd 1 or 2 under a 64 KiB budget; a line larger than the remaining budget is silently dropped and zeroes the budget.
Twelve per-run limits with defaults, overridable per runner or per run. CPU and wall time are separate; the interrupt handler checks both.

Fresh QuickJS context per run. Continuations: a host function can interrupt (for approval or auth), and the run resumes later by replaying the source with a ledger of recorded host results, so completed host calls are not repeated. Date and Math.random are deterministic in the guest to make replay consistent.

Guest errors keep name, message and a guest stack with run.js line:column. Host function errors are replaced by "Host function failed." unless the host throws a RunError, so host secrets in error text stay on the host side.

Process-wide worker cap (setMaxWorkers, default from available memory up to 32). Signed or stored continuation codecs. A fail-closed banned-pattern security scan runs in CI. Labs experiment status, Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-11-12.

surprises: console.log output never reaches the caller. It goes to the host server's stdout, so in an agent it lands in server logs and the model never sees it.
A console.log line bigger than the remaining 64 KiB budget is dropped whole, with no marker, and later lines in the same run are dropped too.
Going over maxInFlightBridgeRequests fails the whole run instead of queueing; in P9b, 32 host calls had already executed when the run failed.
Guest Date.now() is deterministic for replay, but it still advanced across host awaits in P9 (259 ms), so in-guest timing is usable.
